details: Grayscale's Head of Research, Zach Pandl, stated on August 9, 2026, that the CLARITY Act, a bill intended to establish US rules for digital asset markets, is unlikely to pass in 2026. A Senate floor vote is anticipated after lawmakers return on September 15. Pandl expects the SEC and other regulators to address existing gaps through rulemaking, particularly concerning tokenized securities. He also acknowledged progress in institutional custody, staking policy clarity, and the growth of crypto ETPs. However, Pandl warned that this delay could divert new investment and developer activity overseas, potentially hindering US crypto adoption and market growth.
title: US Senate's CLARITY Act Unlikely to Pass in 2026

details: The July U.S. employment report, released on August 8, 2026, showed a loss of 23,000 jobs, significantly missing expectations for a gain of approximately 80,000. This weaker labor data has reduced near-term expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes, fostering a broader rally in risk assets, including cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin has seen structural support from this development, contributing to its recovery.
title: Weak US Jobs Report Boosts Risk Assets, Including Bitcoin

details: U.S. spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) recorded $853.54 million in net inflows for the week ending August 7, 2026, marking the largest weekly inflow since mid-April. BlackRock's IBIT fund accounted for the majority of this surge, demonstrating renewed institutional demand and providing structural support to the cryptocurrency market.
title: Bitcoin Spot ETFs Experience Significant Inflows

details: Over 100 crypto projects have either shut down, filed for bankruptcy, or gone permanently dark in 2026, with the pace accelerating. This trend, described as a "massive dot-com style shakeout," spans across various sectors including exchanges, wallets, DeFi lending protocols, NFT marketplaces, and layer-1 blockchains. The industry is experiencing a consolidation phase, with observers noting that capital is becoming more selective, and projects without proven market fit are failing. Furthermore, the first half of 2026 saw $1.1 billion lost to on-chain exploits, exceeding all of 2025 combined.
title: Crypto Industry Undergoing Significant Shakeout

details: Michael Saylor's MicroStrategy is reportedly shifting its Bitcoin strategy, selling 1,638 Bitcoin to raise $104.7 million to bolster its USD Reserve for preferred stock dividends. This marks a pivot from the company's long-standing "buy and hold, forever" approach, as it now prioritizes maintaining dividend obligations for its Digital Credit Framework over simply accumulating Bitcoin for shareholders.
title: MicroStrategy Sells Bitcoin to Fund Preferred Stock Dividends
